title: How to organize the detergent and treatment zone | Laundry Room
description:
Hold the chemistry that actually gets used, at a dose you can measure and out of a child's reach.

This is the Detergent and Treatment Zone in the Laundry Room. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
One working detergent, one bleach, one tub of oxygen powder and one stain treatment standing on a wipeable tray, the pod tub latched and above shoulder height, the true dose line inked on the cap, and not one unlabeled bottle on the shelf.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Line every bottle, stick, spray and pod tub up on the floor.
Straighten: The everyday detergent and its dosing cap sit within arm's reach of the open washer lid, because that is where
Shine: Detergent drips, always.
Safety: Bleach and any ammonia based cleaner never share a shelf, and never share a bucket.
Standardize: Mark the true dose line on the cap with a permanent marker, since the moulded cap is bigger than the dose almo
Sustain: When you pour the last dose out of a jug, the empty goes straight to recycling and the replacement goes on the

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
One product per job, standing on a tray, with the real dose line marked on the cap.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/laundry-room-the-detergent-and-treatment-zone.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
